source.title: Neural Optimizer Search with Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Irwan Bello; Barret Zoph; Vijay Vasudevan; Quoc V. Le

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer choices using held-out test accuracy and perplexity on several tasks, a different set of models and tuning setups from the version's cited studies.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on Wide ResNet/CIFAR-10 and PTB that bear on adaptive optimizers versus SGD. ImageNet and GNMT compare the paper's proposed optimizers with RMSProp or Adam but do not compare adaptive methods with SGD; those results do not test V4. Rosenbrock-function results are not neural-network generalization results.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out Wide ResNet/CIFAR-10 accuracy and PTB language-model perplexity, testing V4 in new model and training settings. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that discovered PowerSign and AddSign update equations transfer across tasks and achieve competitive performance, and that linear cosine decay generally accelerates convergence. Their PTB results favor Adam, with an explicit caveat that Adam-informed hyperparameter ranges may disadvantage the alternatives.
record.recipe_differences: The paper compares optimizers on its own Wide ResNet/CIFAR-10 and PTB setups; it does not reproduce the cited optimizer studies' benchmarks or tuning protocol. It reports learning-rate sweeps and, for some comparisons, cosine decay.
record.method_sensitivity: The Wide ResNet comparison changes with learning-rate decay: the no-decay test accuracies differ only slightly, while the cosine-decay results show larger gaps. The PTB comparison favors Adam over SGD.
record.problems: No error bars or significance tests are reported for the extracted comparisons. Wide ResNet results are averaged over 5 runs, but run-to-run uncertainty is not quantified. The authors state that PTB hyperparameter ranges were manually tuned by experimenting with Adam first, which could negatively affect SGD and their optimizers.
record.rows_left_out: ImageNet Table 3 and GNMT Table 4 compare the proposed optimizers with RMSProp or Adam but do not compare adaptive optimizers against SGD. Rosenbrock Figure 5 is an optimization-function comparison, not a neural-network generalization result. Other proposed-optimizer results are outside V4.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matching architectures and recipes.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning restriction; controlled changes in tuning breadth; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; and whether adaptive methods generalize worse despite equal or better training performance.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove batch penalties.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

missing.what: Table 1 final accuracy: Adam 92.3%, RMSProp 91.6%, SGD 92.3%, Momentum 92.2%. These reveal that Adam's best-accuracy deficit disappears at the final endpoint, while RMSProp remains 0.7 points below SGD.
Momentum comparisons: without decay, best accuracy 93.0%; with cosine decay, final accuracy 95.1%, versus Adam 93.8% and RMSProp 93.5%. Momentum SGD is explicitly part of V4.

Appendix standard-optimizer comparisons: final test accuracy SGD 91.8%, Momentum 92.1%, Adam 90.1%, RMSProp 90.3%; test accuracy at the best-validation checkpoint respectively 91.9%, 92.3%, 90.7%, 90.3%. Seven learning rates were compared using validation accuracy, without decay.

record.verdict_notes: No significance tests or run-level uncertainty establish whether the small no-decay differences are reliable. CIFAR-10 comparisons include weight-decay tuning, and PTB includes substantially broader tuning, so neither isolates V4's restricted tuning protocol. PTB's Adam advantage is already accommodated by V4. Proposed-optimizer-only comparisons and Rosenbrock results do not establish additional claim-version tests.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width beyond interpolation and test-error trends.
The study does not test the cited broader-tuning reversal, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, or the wider set of image and language benchmarks described in the version.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
